frontMatter.welcome:
We’re excited to welcome you to the Transpek Industry Limited family! Your contributions are vital to our growth and success, and we value the unique skills and perspectives you bring to the table.

frontMatter.about:
Transpek Industry Limited, established in 1965, has grown to become one of the most trusted names in the chemical manufacturing industry, with a focus on delivering innovative and sustainable solutions. Our legacy is built on a steadfast commitment to quality, safety, and environmental responsibility.
With state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities and a strong global footprint, we proudly serve industries and businesses in over 50 countries. Our portfolio includes a wide range of specialty chemicals, intermediates, and customized solutions that cater to diverse industrial needs.
Our success stems from a relentless pursuit of technological excellence and sustainable practices. By adhering to international safety and environmental standards, Transpek Industry Limited continues to lead the chemical industry, setting benchmarks for innovation and responsibility.

If you have any queries or need additional clarification, please don’t hesitate to reach out to your manager or the Human Resources team. This handbook is a valuable tool to ensure a smooth and fulfilling career at Transpek Industry Limited.

chapters.title: Environmental Sustainability:
chapters.text:
- Resource Optimization: We aim to reduce the consumption of water, energy, and raw materials through the adoption of efficient technologies and sustainable practices.
- Waste Management: We promote recycling and safe waste disposal, ensuring minimal environmental impact from our operations.
- Pollution Prevention: Advanced pollution control measures are implemented to reduce emissions and manage the environmental footprint of our business activities.
- Sustainable Product Lifecycle: A life-cycle approach is used to assess and minimize the environmental impact of our products, from design through to disposal.
## Health and Safety Commitment:
- Employee Safety: The safety and well-being of our workforce are top priorities. We provide necessary protective equipment, conduct regular safety training, and follow strict safety protocols to minimize risks.
- Risk Management: Potential hazards are identified and mitigated through proactive measures, ensuring a safe working environment for all employees.
- Health and Wellness Programs: We support the physical and mental health of our employees by offering health benefits, ergonomic support, and mental health resources to encourage a balanced lifestyle.
## Ergonomic Workplace Practices:
- The Company promotes ergonomic workplace practices to help minimize the risk of musculoskeletal disorders, repetitive strain injuries, and other work-related discomfort arising from repetitive movements, manual handling, or prolonged working postures.
- Workstations, tools, equipment, and work processes are reviewed, where practicable, to support safe and comfortable working conditions based on the nature of the work performed.
- Employees are encouraged to use proper working techniques, maintain correct posture, and promptly report any ergonomic concerns or physical discomfort to their immediate supervisor or the Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) team.
- Where appropriate, suitable workplace adjustments, job rotation, or other reasonable measures may be implemented to help reduce ergonomic risks and improve employee comfort and well-being.
## Psychological Well-being and Stress Management:
- The Company recognizes the importance of promoting employees' psychological well-being and encourages a supportive and respectful work environment that helps minimize work-related stress.
- Employees are encouraged to discuss work-related concerns, excessive workload, or other factors affecting their well-being with their immediate supervisor or the Human Resources department so that appropriate support can be provided, where feasible.
- The Company may conduct awareness programmes, training sessions, or communication initiatives to promote mental well-being, stress management, and a positive workplace culture.
- Where appropriate, the Company will review reported concerns and consider reasonable measures to help address workplace factors that may contribute to stress or affect employees' psychological well-being.
- Emergency Preparedness: Clear emergency procedures are in place to ensure a swift and effective response in case of accidents or health emergencies.
- Hazardous Substance Control: Active control measures are in place to prevent employees from exposure to hazardous substances in the workplace, including ventilation and extraction systems, job rotation to limit contact, and clear work instructions for safe chemical handling.
- Noise Exposure Prevention: We mitigate occupational noise exposure through regular noise measurements, noise-cancelling equipment, and mandatory hearing protection in designated high-noise areas.
- Radiation Exposure Control: Where relevant to operations, employees are protected through radiation protection programs, personal exposure monitoring, and safety instructions to reduce risk of exposure to ionizing radiation.
## Site Safety Requirements
The Company is committed to maintaining a safe working environment for everyone present at its premises, including contractors, subcontractors, temporary workers, service providers, and visitors performing authorized work.
## Safety Orientation:
Where applicable, contractors and other non-employee workers are provided with relevant site safety instructions before commencing work to ensure they are aware of workplace hazards, emergency procedures, and applicable safety requirements.
## Safe Work Practices:
Contractors and other non-employee workers are expected to comply with Company safety rules, use the required personal protective equipment (PPE), and perform their work in accordance with applicable safety procedures.

chapters.title: Risk Awareness and Emergency Preparedness:
chapters.text:
Appropriate safety precautions shall be followed for activities carried out by non-employee workers. Contractors are expected to cooperate with the Company during emergency situations and follow site emergency response procedures and evacuation instructions.
## Reporting of Safety Concerns:
Any unsafe condition, incident, injury, or near miss observed by contractors or other non-employee workers should be reported promptly to the designated Company representative or site supervisor for appropriate action.
## Excessive Use of Force and Freedom of Movement Restrictions
## Prohibition of Excessive Force by Security Personnel:
- Zero-Tolerance Policy: Security personnel employed or contracted by Transpek Industry Limited are strictly prohibited from using excessive force or engaging in actions that may harm employees, visitors, or any other individuals.
- Specialized Training: All security staff undergo comprehensive training in conflict resolution and de-escalation techniques to handle challenging situations professionally and calmly.
- Incident Reporting: Any suspected misuse of force by security personnel must be reported immediately through the designated reporting channels. Such reports will be investigated promptly, and appropriate actions will be taken..

chapters.title: Freedom of Movement:
chapters.text:
- Employee Rights: All employees have the right to move freely within their designated workspaces. Restrictions may only be applied when necessary for security or operational safety reasons.
- Grievance Mechanism: If an employee believes their freedom of movement has been unfairly restricted, they are encouraged to file a grievance. All complaints will be thoroughly reviewed and investigated to ensure fairness and resolution.
## Occupational Health & Safety Incident Reporting
To maintain a safe and healthy workplace, all employees are encouraged to promptly report occupational health and safety incidents, hazards, near misses, unsafe conditions, and any other safety concerns.
## Reporting of Incidents and Hazards:
- Employees should immediately report any work-related injury, illness, near miss, unsafe condition, or health and safety concern to their immediate supervisor, Department Head, Human Resources, or the Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) team, as applicable.
- Prompt reporting enables the Company to assess risks, take appropriate corrective actions, and help prevent similar incidents from occurring.
## nvestigation and Corrective Actions:
- All reported occupational health and safety incidents and concerns are reviewed and investigated, where appropriate, to identify the cause and determine suitable corrective and preventive actions.
- Employees are expected to cooperate during investigations and support the implementation of approved corrective measures.
## Record Keeping:
- The Company maintains records of reported occupational health and safety incidents, investigations, and corrective actions in accordance with applicable legal requirements and internal procedures.
- These records are reviewed periodically to identify trends and opportunities for continual improvement in workplace health and safety.
## Protection Against Retaliation:
- Employees who report health and safety concerns in good faith will not be subjected to retaliation or unfair treatment.
- All employees are encouraged to raise genuine safety concerns to help maintain a safe working environment for everyone.

## Recruitment Process: Transparent and Inclusive Hiring Steps
Transpek Industry Limited follows a structured, transparent, and inclusive recruitment process to ensure fairness and equal opportunities for all. Our recruitment approach is designed to attract skilled talent, support organizational goals, and promote a culture of professionalism and excellence.
## dentifying the Requirement for New Talent
- Initiating the Process :
- Departments identifying the need for new roles or replacements submit a Manpower Requisition Form (MRF) to the HR department.
- The MRF includes details such as job title, responsibilities, qualifications, experience, and justification for the role.
## Approval Process:
- The HR Business Partner reviews the MRF to validate the necessity of the position and ensure its alignment with company objectives.
- After initial validation, the request is escalated to the manageging director and joint managing director for final approval
## Advertising Job Openings
## nternal Job Postings:
- Job opportunities are first announced internally through email notifications and notice board. This encourages existing employees to apply and grow withing the organization.
## External Job Advertisements:
- If no suitable internal candidates are found, roles are advertised externally via job portals, the Transpek careers page, LinkedIn, recruitment agencies, or through campus placements.
## Diversity and Inclusion:
- All job advertisements include a statement emphasizing Transpek’s commitment to diversity and equal opportunity.
- Applications are encouraged from individuals of all genders, ages, backgrounds, and abilities.
## Reviewing Applications
- Screening Process: The Talent Acquisition (TA) Team thoroughly reviews applications to ensure candidates meet the required qualifications and experience.
- Shortlisting: Eligible candidates are shortlisted for the next stages of the recruitment process.
## nterview Process
## nterview Panel Composition:
- HOD or Reporting Manager: Assesses the candidate’s technical expertise and job-specific skills.
- HR Representative: Evaluates cultural fit, teamwork capabilities, and alignment with Transpek’s values.
- TA Representative: Ensures the process is consistent and unbiased.
## nterviewer Responsibilities
- HR Representatives and interview panel members are expected to conduct interviews objectively and consistently using predefined evaluation criteria.
- Interviewers are periodically briefed on equal employment opportunity principles, unconscious bias awareness, and non-discriminatory recruitment practices.
## nterview Rounds:
- Technical Round: Focuses on assessing the candidate’s core skills and problem-solving abilities.

## Compensation, Benefits, and Career Path Guidelines
At Transpek Industry Limited, we are dedicated to creating an equitable and growth-oriented work environment. Our compensation policies and career advancement initiatives reflect our commitment to fairness, transparency, and employee development, ensuring everyone has the opportunity to thrive and excel.
## Comprehensive Compensation Structure
1. Core Principles:
- Fair Compensation: Employees are paid above statutory minimum wage as mandated by government regulations.
- Equitable Practices: Salary decisions are transparent and based on market benchmarks, job responsibilities, and individual performance.
- Sustainability Focus: Compensation frameworks balance competitiveness with long-term organizational growth.
2. Compensation Components:
- Base Salary: Reflects the role’s requirements and responsibilities.
- Performance Incentives: Bonuses are directly linked to individual, team, and company performance.
- Statutory and Other Benefits: Includes Provident Fund, Gratuity, Superannuation, HRA, and Commutation allowances to ensure employees’ financial stability.
3. Market Competitiveness:
- Annual reviews compare salaries with industry standards to attract and retain top talent.
4. Compensation Determinants:
- Alignment of the role with organizational objectives.
- Employee skills, experience, and qualifications.
- Performance metrics and individual contributions.
- Internal pay equity and industry trends.
## Annual Salary Review Process
1. Revision Cycle:
- Annual Review: The salary revision process is conducted annually, effective from April 1, to reflect employee performance and contributions during the preceding financial year (April–March).
- Consistency: This cycle ensures employees are consistently rewarded and acknowledged for their efforts, fostering motivation and alignment with organizational goals.
2. Eligibility Criteria:
- Joining Criteria: Employees who joined the company before September 30 of the financial year are included in the salary revision cycle.
- Exclusion for Probationary Staff: Employees still on probation as of the review date may not qualify
## Performance-Linked Revisions:
- Evaluation Process: Salary increments are determined by appraisal ratings derived from standardized evaluation tools and KPIs.

chapters.title: Overtime Compensation:
chapters.text:
- Overtime is compensated as per releveant Act, the standard hourly rate, ensuring fair remuneration for extra work.
## Compensatory Leave:
- Leave Option: Employees of officer may choose compensatory leave instead of extra hours pay, based on operational feasibility. While Sr. Officer to Dy. Manager level employees can only avail Compensatory leave.
- Approval Process: Compensatory leave requests must be approved by department heads in advance.
## Approval Process:
- Pre-Approval Mandatory: Overtime must be pre-approved to qualify for compensation or leave.
- Exception Handling: Emergency overtime is documented for subsequent approval and payment.
## Career Development and Promotion Policy
1. Merit-Based Promotions:
- Promotions are awarded based on individual performance, potential, and organizational requirements.
- Annual performance appraisals are the primary basis for promotion decisions.
2. Promotion Criteria:
- High performance in achieving KPIs and exceeding role expectations.
- Feedback from supervisors and department heads.
- Demonstrated alignment with Transpek’s values and adherence to safety standards.
3. Leadership Development:
- High-potential employees are identified for Leadership Development Programs, preparing them for future managerial or strategic roles.
4. Promotion Timing:
- Promotions are typically evaluated during the annual appraisal cycle but may occur mid-year for exceptional performers.
5. Transition Support:
- Employees promoted to new roles receive tailored training, mentorship, and onboarding to ensure a smooth transition and success in their new responsibilities.
## nternal Career Mobility
1. Vertical Growth:
- Employees are encouraged to advance to higher positions within their functional area. Career advancement pathways are well-defined and communicated during appraisals.
2. Horizontal Mobility:
- Cross-departmental transfers allow employees to diversify their skills and broaden their career prospects.
- Eligible employees are compensated for approved overtime at double the standard hourly rate. Overtime details are transparently displayed in the HR portal.
## D. Leave and Time-Off Integration
## Leave Balances:
- Employees can track their leave balances (annual leave, sick leave, etc.) in real-time via the HR portal.
## Leave Deductions:
- Approved leave is automatically reflected in payroll calculations, ensuring accuracy in salary adjustments for any unpaid leave.
## Transparent Approval Process:
- Leave requests and their approval status can be monitored through the portal, maintaining clear communication between employees and managers.
## E. Payroll Process
## Salary Payments:
- Salaries are processed monthly and directly credited to employees’ bank accounts on or before 7th of each month.
## Payslip Details:
- Monthly payslips include a breakup of:
- Basic salary.
- Allowances (e.g., HRA, commutation allowance, medical allowance, etc).
- Deductions (e.g., taxes, Provident Fund, professional tax, canteen deduction, medical claim).
- Payslips are available for download through the HR portal.
## Deductions Transparency:
- All statutory and voluntary deductions are clearly itemized on payslips, ensuring employees understand the components of their net pay.
## F. Remuneration Review and Feedback
## Annual Salary Review:
- Transpek conducts an annual review of all remuneration packages to ensure competitiveness and fairness. Salary adjustments are communicated transparently during performance evaluations and updated on the HR portal.
## Employee Feedback Mechanism:
- Employees are encouraged to share feedback on remuneration practices through surveys or direct discussions with HR. This input helps refine and improve the compensation framework.
## G. Equal Pay for Equal Work
## Commitment to Non-Discrimination:
- Transpek strictly adheres to the principle of equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender, ethnicity, religion, or other personal attributes.
## Regular Pay Audits:
- Annual audits ensure compliance with equal pay policies, and any identified disparities are addressed promptly.
## Guidelines for Advancement:
- Clear policies regarding promotions, salary adjustments, and role-based pay are accessible through the HR portal, enabling employees to understand their career progression.
## H. Periodic Review of Compensation
- The Company periodically reviews its compensation practices to help ensure that employee wages remain fair, competitive, and aligned with business requirements, applicable legal provisions, and prevailing market conditions.
- During such reviews, the Company may consider relevant factors including employee roles and responsibilities, individual performance, business performance, industry compensation practices, and other economic considerations, where appropriate.
- Any revisions to employee compensation are implemented in accordance with the Company's remuneration practices and applicable statutory requirements.

## Transpek Leave Policy: A Comprehensive Guide
At Transpek Industry Limited, our compensation framework and career advancement policies aim to foster a culture of fairness, reward excellence, and promote professional growth. These policies ensure that employees are fairly compensated, evaluated transparently, and provided with opportunities for meaningful career progression.
## A. Leave Types and Entitlements
## Annual Leave (Earned Leave):
## Eligibility:
- Employees are entitled to annual leave after completing minimum 20 days of continuous service.
## Entitlement:
- 21 days of annual leave per calendar year.
- Accrual is calculated on a pro-rata basis, and employees can carry forward unused annual leave up to a maximum of 60 days.
## Approval Process:
- Leave applications must be applied in advance and approved by the reporting manager.
## Casual Leave:
## Eligibility:
- All employees are eligible for casual leave from their first month of employment. But CL will be credited into their leave balance only after their completion of 45 days from joining.
## Entitlement:
- 7 days of casual leave per year.
- Accrual is calculated on a pro-rate basis
## Conditions:
- Casual leave cannot be carried forward or encashed.
## Sick Leave:
## Eligibility:
- Employees are entitled to paid sick leave from their first month of employment.
## Entitlement:
- 7 days of sick leave per year.
- Accrual is calculated on a pro-rata basis, and employees can carry forward unused annual leave up to a maximum of 50 days.
## Conditions:
- Employees are required to notify their manager on the first day of absence.
- For absences exceeding 3 or more consecutive days, a medical certificate must be submitted.
- Unused sick leave cannot be carried forwarded.

chapters.title: Maternity Leave:
chapters.text:
## Eligibility:
- Female employees who have completed at least 80 days of service before the expected delivery date are eligible.
## Entitlement:
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave for the third child and beyond.
## Additional Leave:
- Female employees experiencing complications related to pregnancy, miscarriage, or medical termination are entitled to additional weeks of leave on medical grounds subject to MD's approval.
## Eligibility:
- Male employees with at least 6 months of service are eligible.
## Entitlement:
- 5 days of paid leave to be taken within 3 months of childbirth.
## Special Leave (Natural Calamities or Critical Medical Emergency):
## Eligibility:
- Employees are eligible for special leave subject to prior approval of Managing Director.
## Entitlement:
- Depending on the nature of circumstances Special Leave may be granted completed based on Managing Director's approval.
## Compensatory Leave:
## Eligibility:
- Officer to Dy. Manager level Employees working extra hours normal duty day, or public holidays or rest days are eligible for compensatory leave.
## Entitlement:
- One day of leave for every 8 hours of extra work and Half day of leave for every 4 hours of extra work. Subject to Head of department's approval.
## B. Public Holidays
- Employees are entitled to 6 public holidays declared by the government of their respective work location. (i.e. Uttarayan, Republic Day, Raksha Bandhan, Independence Day, New Year and Bhai Bij)
- If a public holiday falls on a weekend, special leave will be provided as per Managing Director's prior approval.
## C. Leave Encashment Policy
## Annual Leave Encashment:
- Employees will be eligible for leave encashment in the month of January, only for the nos. of leaves lapsed, maximum subject to 50% of leaves credited in the beginning of the year.
## Encashment at Separation:
- Unused earned leave (annual leave) will be encashed at the time of resignation, retirement, or death, calculated based on the last drawn basic + DA (if applicable) salary.
- Sick leave will be encashed at the time of retirement & death.
## Non- Encashable Leave:
- Sick leave and casual leave cannot be encashed.
## D. Leave Application Process
## Submission:
- All leave requests must be applied online through the HRMS portal.
## Approval:
- Approval is required from the immediate supervisor or reporting manager.
## Documentation:
- For sick leave exceeding 2 days, a medical certificate must be submitted within 2 days of resuming work.
- For maternity leave, a doctor’s certificate is required.
## E. Unplanned or Emergency Leave
- Employees must inform their reporting manager immediately if unable to report to work due to unforeseen circumstances.
- In such cases, leave will be adjusted from available casual or sick leave balances.
## G. Leave Audits and Monitoring
## Leave Balance Updates:
- Employees can view their leave balances in real time via the HR portal.
## Monitoring and Compliance:
- HR conducts periodic leave audits to ensure compliance with policies and minimize misuse.
## Regularization of Unauthorized Absences:
- Employees with unauthorized absences must meet with their manager and HR to regularize their status.
By establishing these comprehensive leave policies, Transpek Industry Limited ensures that employees can meet their personal and professional obligations, contributing to a supportive and productive workplace.
## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy
At Transpek Industry Limited, we prioritize maintaining an efficient and accountable work environment while ensuring that employees can manage their time effectively. The Attendance and Working Hours Policy is designed to balance business requirements with individual needs, providing a structure that ensures consistency and transparency in attendance management.
## A. Working Hours Policy
## Standard Working Hours:
- The standard working hours at Transpek Industry Limited are 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Saturday, with a 0.30-hour lunch break from 11:45 PM to 1:45 PM.
## Core Hours:
- Core working hours are from 08:30 AM to 5:00 PM, during which all employees are expected to be available for meetings, collaborations, and communication.
## B. Attendance Recording
## Attendance System:
- Transpek employs an automated biometric attendance system for all employees. Employees are required to clock in and out at the beginning and end of each working day to ensure accurate recording of work hours.
- For remote work, attendance is tracked through the attendance registar using a daily check-in/check-out system.
## Late Arrival or Early Departure:
- Employees are expected to arrive on time and adhere to their designated working hours.
- Any late arrivals or early departures must be recorded in the attendance system and justified with valid reasons (e.g., medical, family emergency).
- Repeated tardiness may lead to disciplinary action after multiple warnings.

## Employee Provident Fund (EPF) & Employee Pension Scheme (EPS)
At Transpek Industry Limited, we prioritize the financial well-being and long-term security of our employees. As part of this commitment, we provide statutory benefits such as the Employee Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS) in compliance with the Employees' Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. These schemes ensure that employees have a secure savings foundation for their post-retirement life and unforeseen contingencies.
## A. Employee Provident Fund (EPF)
The EPF is a savings scheme designed to provide employees with financial stability during their post-employment years.
## Eligibility and Coverage:
- All employees earning are mandatorily covered under EPF.
## Contribution Structure:
- Employee Contribution: Employees contribute 12% of their basic salary + dearness allowance (DA) to the EPF account. If basic pay + DA is less that 15000?- then, as per basic wage definition of PF Act.
## Employer Contribution:
- The employer matches the employee’s contribution of 12%, out of which 8.33% is directed to the EPS, and the remaining 3.67% goes to the EPF account.
## Interest and Returns:
- The EPF account earns annual interest as determined by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
- The interest is compounded annually and credited to the employee’s account at the end of each financial year by EPFO office.
## Benefits of EPF:
- Savings Growth: Contributions grow over time with compound interest.
- Partial Withdrawals: Employees can make partial withdrawals for specific purposes, such as:
- Marriage or education.
- Medical emergencies.
- Home construction or purchase.
- Tax-Free Returns: EPF contributions and withdrawals (after 5 years of continuous service) are exempt from income tax under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
## Withdrawal Process:
- Employees can withdraw their EPF balance upon:
- Resignation or retirement.
- Withdrawals can be made via the Unified Portal of EPFO using the employee’s UAN (Universal Account Number).

The EPS is a pension benefit aimed at providing employees with a steady income post-retirement.

## Two-Way Communication Policy
At Transpek Industry Limited, we value open dialogue between employees and management as a cornerstone of an inclusive and collaborative workplace. This policy aims to establish structured, interactive communication channels that allow employees to share feedback, raise concerns, and contribute ideas while providing management with an opportunity to respond directly, clarify decisions, and foster transparency.
## A. Objective
The purpose of this policy is to facilitate meaningful two-way communication between employees and management at all levels. Through regular communication sessions, we aim to:
- Create an environment of openness and trust.
- Address concerns related to working conditions, benefits, or organizational changes.
- Provide a platform for employees to contribute ideas for operational and cultural improvements.
- Strengthen the alignment of individual and organizational goals.
## B. Scope
This policy applies to all employees of Transpek Industry Limited, including full-time, part-time, and contractual staff, as well as managers and senior leadership. It ensures organization-wide inclusivity, promoting engagement at every level.
## C. Responsibility
## Human Resources (HR):
- Organize, facilitate, and document communication sessions.
- Provide resources and training to managers for effective communication.
## Managers and Team Leaders:
- Encourage participation from their respective teams.
- Address team-specific concerns during departmental feedback sessions.
## Leadership Team:
- Actively participate in company-wide forums and Q&A sessions.
- Respond to employee feedback with transparency and accountability.

## Departmental Feedback Sessions:

chapters.title: Training & Development
chapters.text:
At Transpek Industry Limited, we prioritize equipping our workforce with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to excel in their roles. This policy provides a structured approach to identifying, planning, and executing training programs tailored to individual, departmental, and organizational needs. It also fosters a supportive environment where continuous learning and personal development are actively encouraged.
## A. Objective
The objective of the Training & Development Policy is to:
- Enhance Role-Specific Skills: Equip employees with the necessary competencies to perform their duties effectively, focusing on Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and technical proficiency.
- Promote Continuous Learning: Ensure ongoing professional growth through structured training, mentorship, and skill development programs.
- Support Workplace Excellence: Improve operational efficiency, compliance, and innovation across all functions.
- Foster Work-Life Balance and Well-Being: Provide training programs addressing repetitive strain, stress management, and family support for a healthier work environment.
## B. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, including:
- Permanent Staff and workers: Employees working in manufacturing, quality assurance, engineering, and support functions.
- Contractual Staff: Temporary or project-based employees requiring functional training.
- New Hires and Existing Employees: Employees undergoing induction or skill enhancement programs.
## C. Roles and Responsibilities
## Training Coordinator:
- Oversees the development, execution, and tracking of training programs.
- Manages cGMP training schedules for relevant departments.
- Ensures timely delivery of on-the-job training for new hires.
- Coordinates with department heads to address training gaps.
## Department Training Coordinators:
- Identify departmental training needs, particularly around Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Monitor employee progress and ensure timely completion of assigned training modules.
## Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
- Conduct training sessions, offering in-depth knowledge of their respective domains.
- Facilitate hands-on, practical learning experiences.
## Human Resources (HR):
- Organizes induction training programs for all new hires.
- Ensures seamless onboarding by aligning training content with company goals.
- Tracks training compliance and collects feedback for continuous improvement.
## Employees:
- Actively participate in training sessions and complete assigned modules within the specified timelines.
- Apply learned skills to their daily responsibilities and share feedback to enhance training effectiveness.
## D. Training Procedures
## Training Needs Identification (TNI):
- Conducted annually to assess skill gaps and align training programs with organizational objectives.
- Department heads collaborate with HR to document and address role-specific training needs.
## nduction Training:
- Purpose: Introduce new employees to the company’s mission, vision, policies, and safety protocols.
## Content:
- Overview of company operations and core values.
- Departmental orientation and role-specific responsibilities.
## cGMP and Role-Specific Training:
- Employees receive comprehensive training on cGMP standards and job-specific SOPs.
- Practical, on-the-job training is documented to ensure readiness for routine tasks.
## Continuous Professional Development (CPD):
- Programs include certifications, leadership workshops, and cross-functional training to promote career advancement.
## E. Specific Programs
## Women Empowerment and Career Development:
- Mentorship Programs: Pair female employees with senior leaders to provide career guidance and professional advice.
- Sponsorship Initiatives: High-performing women are sponsored for leadership roles, with active advocacy by senior leaders.
- Leadership Development Workshops: Interactive sessions on negotiation, public speaking, and strategic decision-making for women aspiring to leadership roles.
- Networking Events: Provide platforms for female employees to collaborate, share experiences, and learn from peers and mentors
## Stress and Repetitive Strain Prevention:
- Ergonomic Workstations: Adjustable desks, chairs, and accessories to reduce physical strain and enhance posture.
- Regular Stretching Breaks: Scheduled breaks encourage employees to move, stretch, and avoid repetitive motion injuries.
- Educational Workshops: Sessions on maintaining posture, managing stress, and avoiding repetitive strain injuries.
- Job Rotation: Rotate employees across roles to reduce physical or cognitive monotony, preventing burnout and fatigue.
## Employee Resource and Support Groups
- Open Access: Transpek supports the formation of employee resource groups open to all employees, including but not limited to working parents, employees from different cultural and religious backgrounds, and other affinity groups based on shared interests or identities.

## Records Retention and Management Framework
At Transpek Industry Limited, we understand the importance of effective record retention and management in ensuring compliance, operational efficiency, and confidentiality. Our detailed Records Retention Framework outlines the systematic handling of all employee, third-party, and organizational records. This ensures that essential information is maintained securely, accessible when required, and disposed of responsibly after its retention period.
## A. Objective of Records Retention Framework
The primary objectives of this framework include:
- Ensuring legal and regulatory compliance with applicable laws, including labor laws, tax regulations, and data protection laws.
- Supporting operational continuity through the preservation of critical records and data.
- Protecting confidentiality and maintaining the integrity of sensitive information.
- Optimizing storage efficiency and reducing unnecessary retention of obsolete records.
## B. Scope
The Records Retention Framework applies to:
- Employee Records: Including personnel files, payroll data, and performance reviews.
- Third-Party Data: Contracts, agreements, and correspondence with vendors, customers, and suppliers.
- Organizational Records: Financial statements, audit reports, and legal compliance documentation.
## C. Key Principles of Records Management
## Retention Period Compliance:
- Records are retained for specified periods as mandated by law, contracts, or internal policies.
## Confidentiality and Security:
- Sensitive records are stored with access controls, encryption, and regular audits to prevent unauthorized access.
## Ease of Retrieval:
- Documents are categorized and indexed for quick and efficient retrieval.
## Responsible Disposal:
- Records that exceed their retention period are destroyed securely using certified methods.
## D. Comprehensive Records Retention Schedule
The following table outlines retention periods for various record categories:
[table]
| Record Type | Retention Period | Responsible Department | Retention Method |
| Employee Records |
| Offer Letters & Contracts | 7 years after separation | Human Resources | Encrypted digital storage and archives |
| Payroll Data | 8 years | Human Resources | HR/payroll management system |
| Performance Reviews | 5 years after separation | Human Resources | Secure physical and digital archives |
| Health & Safety Training Records | Duration of employment + 3 years | Human Resources | HRIS and digital storage |
## E. Document Disposal and Destruction
## Secure Disposal Methods:
- Physical Records: Shredding, incineration, or disposal by authorized vendors.
- Electronic Records: Deletion through certified software tools that prevent data recovery.
## F. Retention for Employee
## Employee Information Retention:
- Medical Records: Retained for 3 years post-separation to support potential claims or regulatory audits.
- Training Records: Retained for 3 years post-employment to ensure compliance with operational standards.
## G. Roles and Responsibilities
## Human Resources Department:
- Manages employee-related records, including payroll, performance reviews, and training documents.
## Legal and Compliance Team:
- Ensures adherence to statutory retention periods and oversees the management of sensitive legal data.
## T Department:
- Maintains secure storage systems, facilitates data encryption, and ensures reliable backup mechanisms.
## Department Heads:
- Oversee record retention within their teams, ensuring compliance with company standards.
## H. Record Retention for Accessibility and Inclusion
## Accessible Infrastructure:
- Ensure all employees, including those with disabilities, can access relevant personal documents through user-friendly interfaces.
## Digital Transformation:
- Employ cloud-based systems and digital workflows to enhance accessibility and reduce physical storage dependencies.
## Communication and Training
## Employee Awareness Campaigns:
- Employees are briefed on records retention policies during onboarding and receive periodic updates on any changes.
## Training for Key Personnel:
- HR and administrative staff are trained on secure storage, timely disposal, and record retrieval processes.
## J. Benefits of a Records Retention Framework
## Legal Compliance:
- Ensures adherence to statutory obligations, reducing legal risks.
## Operational Efficiency:
- Streamlined record retrieval processes save time and resources.
## Data Security:
- Protects sensitive employee and organizational data through secure storage and controlled access.
## Cost Management:
- Optimizes storage costs by eliminating redundant records.
## Risk Mitigation:
- Reduces risks associated with data breaches or non-compliance through structured policies.
